dod_intent_evidence: Two Air Force STTR Phase II awards in 2022 (~$750k each) explicitly targeting a DAF/Global Strike Command CBRNE and Emergency Management drone use case, plus a 2025 AFWERX contract to scale BVLOS sensing — SBIR abstract section and news section.
score_evidence: 'point-click-fly capability...faster and more efficient response times, increased situational awareness, improved safety' → lab_language_intensity (mostly operational-benefit framing, not TRL/accuracy brags)

'integrated into the Air Force's existing common UAS control software, Vigilant Spirit' shows real prime/flow-down awareness, but no ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/STIG language anywhere → deployment_awareness_absence held below cap of 12
'Air Force Global Strike Command's EMPO NCOIC became the representative of the need and committed to being our MOU End-User' → operator_absence very low, operators/end-users are central and named

Open roles: 'Head of Sales and Business Development', 'Junior Software Engineer', 'Computer Vision Engineer', 'Technical Writing Intern' — none in field, deployment, compliance, or ISSO roles → hiring_profile_skew

'Lighthouse Avionics to Scale AI-Driven BVLOS Sensing with AFWERX Contract' (2025-08-21) on a 4-13 person venture-backed team already juggling two 2022 STTR Phase IIs and municipal commercial deals → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: Networked-tower architecture assumes connectivity the OCONUS EM use case explicitly denies
blind_spots.operator_reality: Their own SBIR abstract states the CBRNE solution 'will be employed by USAF EM professionals at bases both CONUS and OCONUS,' yet VICTOR's value proposition is a networked, range-limited (10km) tower feeding sensor and Drone ID data back to a control point — the same connectivity assumption that breaks in contested or austere OCONUS basing.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: VICTOR was designed first for municipal police/fire BVLOS programs with reliable cell/network backhaul, then pitched at DoD without re-architecting for degraded links.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: This solution will be employed by USAF EM professionals at bases both CONUS and OCONUS.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Claims Vigilant Spirit integration without any stated ATO/accreditation path
blind_spots.operator_reality: Getting software onto Vigilant Spirit as a common UAS control layer means clearing an Air Force ATO/RMF gate; stating the integration as a project deliverable without naming the accreditation milestone is exactly where a Phase II clock runs out before the network connection is real.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The abstract is written to sell the technical integration achievement to Phase II reviewers, not to map the compliance path that actually gets it live on a government network.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: this project will result in a CBRNE sensor agnostic artificially intelligent autonomous drone which is integrated into the Air Force's existing common UAS control software, Vigilant Spirit

blind_spots.blind_spot: Advocacy chain rests on a single named individual, not an institutional sponsor above operator level
blind_spots.operator_reality: One NCOIC as the sole MOU End-User is a champion, not adoption — if that person rotates out (a near-certainty on a normal DoD assignment cycle), the CBRNE program loses its only named advocate before the fully autonomous drone solution transitions.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: STTR Phase I customer-discovery processes reward finding one enthusiastic stakeholder; the abstract never names a program office or budget line above that individual.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Air Force Global Strike Command's EMPO NCOIC became the representative of the need and committed to being our MOU End-User.

opener_hook: Your Global Strike Command EMPO NCOIC MOU commits the CBRNE drone work to Vigilant Spirit integration — worth comparing notes on what actually gets that from an MOU to a live ATO'd connection.
what_they_do: Builds VICTOR, a ground-based Virtual Control Tower for drone airspace awareness and counter-UAS detection, sold to municipal first responders and adapted under Air Force STTR funding for CBRNE/Emergency Management drone operations.
